requirements.text: The system shall receive configuration information from the EVLA M&C system and translate it into physical correlator hardware configuration tables.
The system shall process and transfer dynamic control data and monitor data including auto correlation products and state counts.
The system shall monitor correlator health and autonomously perform corrective actions to recover from hardware and computing faults.
The system shall provide tools to collect and display auto correlation products for real-time probing.
The system shall implement a Virtual Correlator Interface (VCI) for configuration via the MCCC or a human GUI.
The system shall provide a redundant communication path between the MCCC and CPCC for remote reboot capabilities.
The CMIB shall be capable of reading a 16-bit identifier from the host correlator board for unique IP addressing.
The system shall support unique user identification and authentication for all access attempts.
All login attempts shall be performed in a secure manner using encrypted passwords.
The system shall provide role-based access control where an administrator manages user privileges and system access.
The system shall log all access attempts to the system.
The communication interface between CMIB, MCCC, and CPCC shall use Ethernet at 100 Mbits/sec or better.
The system shall process correlator hardware interrupts in a deterministic fashion to avoid data loss or corruption.
The system shall include hardware-based watchdog timers to trigger autonomous reboots upon system hangs.
The system shall maintain full state information on both primary and secondary MCCC nodes to allow for failover.
The system architecture shall be modular to allow for expansion of I/O, communications, and processing hardware.
The system shall provide a Graphical User Interface (GUI) for remote access to CMCS test software.
The system shall provide externally visible LED indicators on CMIB carrier boards to show operational status.
All computers and peripherals shall be powered through UPS devices capable of signaling power outages to the CMCS.
